analysis.title: UBS Sippel - US Equities: De Grossing, Not De Risking
key_insights: The week's action was a positioning reset rather than broad equity liquidation, similar to the Situational Awareness driven unwind a couple of months ago. High Touch flows picked up in all three regions.
US flows were defensive: Long Onlys finished 36/64 buy/sell and Hedge Funds 42/50/8 buy/sell/short, with persistent long selling and de-grossing but little fresh single stock shorting.

AI/Momentum is the epicenter. Supply was sustained across Semis, Memory and AI infrastructure with virtually no buy-the-dip sponsorship, while Software, defensives and less-crowded exposures absorbed some of the rotation midweek.

The factor reversal was extreme: Memory -16%, Spec Growth -12% and Momentum L/S -8% on the week, versus Consumer Staples +5% and Value L/S +6%. This points to a shift toward Quality/Value over Growth and crowded Momentum.

CoreWeave is a marker for the AI trade. Widening credit concerns move the debate from demand to whether the economics and financing of the buildout can support the next leg of capex. Strong ASML/TSMC datapoints could not clear this concern.
Hedge Fund net exposure is at the 30th percentile while gross is above the 90th percentile on a five-year basis, leaving portfolios vulnerable to more de-grossing if P&L pressure persists.

Breadth under the indices improved as capital moved into under-owned Consumer, Housing, Healthcare and selected Industrials. Short covering moved the pain from crowded longs into prior laggards and helped small caps and equal weight outperform.
Macro amplified the unwind rather than starting it: the inflation/rates shock accelerated systematic selling, and escalating Middle East risk is moving into the volatility complex.

Friday's higher correlation, VIX spike and first 1m/3m VIX inversion in six months suggest hedging demand is broadening beyond AI-specific risk. Friday afternoon weakness was indiscriminate, particularly in Tech, and looked more like ETF/expiry and hedge-roll activity than single-name fundamental selling.

Earnings remain secondary to positioning for now. Credible bank results and supportive AI prints did not overcome existing supply, which raises the bar for upcoming hyperscaler results on cloud revenue, backlog and cash generation.

The near-term setup is fragile rather than outright bearish. Absent bottom-fishing in AI, elevated gross exposure and a stressed volatility curve leave further de-grossing possible, and recent volatility raises questions about the durability of the capital-markets issuance window.

sector_views.rationale: Sustained supply and no buy-the-dip sponsorship. Memory was -16% on the week.
Staples were +5% on the week as defensives absorbed rotation.
Capital moved into these under-owned areas and breadth improved.

earnings_insights: 10.4% of S&P 500 market cap has reported. 3Q expectations are for revenue growth of 12.1% and EPS growth of 26.5% (expectation, not a print).
Reported earnings are beating estimates by 4.1% on aggregate so far, with 75% of companies topping projections.

Over the next 5 trading days, 80 companies representing 13.8% of S&P 500 market cap report, including Netflix, General Electric, Meta Platforms, Tesla, Procter & Gamble and Western Digital (upcoming, not yet reported).
Meta reports a week earlier than normal. The author asks whether it is trying to get ahead of the cap raise crowd.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong ASML/TSMC datapoints, supportive AI prints and credible bank results. Risk is being redistributed, not abandoned.
tension_points.bear_case: CoreWeave credit concerns put the economics and financing of AI capex in question. There is no bottom-fishing in AI, and gross exposure is still above the 90th percentile.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Hyperscaler results that show cloud revenue, backlog and cash generation can validate the scale and financing needs of AI capex.
